short: Attempted handwriting (M04) is a new text-entry action, shown in one participant; label timing (M02) and decoder (M06) are standard and untested against alternatives.
position: The paper changes the use-time action (M04), training label timing (M02) and the decoder (M06) [@willett2021handwriting]. The action matters most: no wiki study dated 2020 or earlier decodes handwriting (Appendix), and the authors show letters are more separable than straight lines (Fig. 4). Its 90 characters per minute at 5.4% error without editing, about 85 correct (inference), more than double the 39.2 correct characters per minute T5 reached by point-and-click with a Kalman-filter decoder [@pandarinath2017communication], so action and decoder change together. All three components are standard: one participant, and neither the HMM labelling nor the RNN is compared with an alternative [@herff2015brain; @sun2020brain2char]. The offline >99% figure is labelled offline; its corpus is unstated and online word error rate was 25.1%. Attempted speech at 62 words per minute [@willett2023speech] and a 110 characters per minute peak in one finger-typing participant [@jude2026bimanual] have since gone further [later].
